newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JAN 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JAN 7.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Turkey, supported by the US and Britain, has noisily protested to Nicosia over its decision to purchase Russian S-300 missiles. A demarche to Moscow has found no sympathy, with Russia saying the missiles are purely for defensive purposes. Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos says Greece stands by Cyprus's decision.
--The Wild West comes to Athens after locals said they would arm themselves following a spate of burglaries in northeastern Attica. Police are seeking a group of four Albanians.
--The message from the new Clinton administration on Greek-Turkish relations is to include Turkey in Europe.
--Ailing conservative opposition New Democracy sails into the Bermuda Triangle as the major protagonists are unlikely to find any points of agreement at their meeting today.

--Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos claims that Turkey is preparing an incursion in the Aegean. Since 1995, the minister says, the Turkish military has defined a change of borders in the Aegean as being in the national interest and has been systematically preparing. Greece, however, Tsohatzopoulos warns, is not about to accept any such questioning of its sovereignty and will greet any challenge more swiftly and decisively than Turkey thinks.
--The Greek police are on full alert to deal with the spate of burglaries that has frightened residents of northeastern Attica into arming themselves.
--Banks are reducing interest rates on deposit accounts but maintaining high rates on credit card lending.

--Today's meeting between New Democracy president Miltiades Evert, his challenger George Souflias and ND deputy president Ioannis Varvitsiotis is probably the most critical in the party's history, and aims to discuss the entire range of issues affecting the conservative opposition. The margins for agreement however, are small.
--The Simitis government is keeping quiet while Turkey threatens Greece and Cyprus over the purchase of Russian missiles. Britain, the US and Israel are supporting Ankara's stance.
